sanskrit: vaśāyā dugdhaṃ pītvā sādhyā vasavaś ca ye | amī bradhnasya viṣṭapi payo asyā upāsate ||
english: Having drunk the milk of the barren cow, the Sādhyas and the Vasus — those who dwell upon the seat of Bradhna revere the milk of this one.

sanskrit: somam enām eke duhre ghṛtam eka upāsate | ya evaṃ viduṣe vaśāṃ dadus te gatās tridivaṃ divaḥ ||
english: Some milk Soma from her, others attend upon her for clarified butter. Those who have given the barren cow to one who knows thus — they have gone to the triple heaven, to the sky.

sanskrit: vaśāṃ dattvā brāhmaṇebhyaḥ sarvāṃl lokān sam aśnute | ṛtaṃ hy asyām āhitam api brahmātho tapaḥ ||
english: By giving the barren cow to Brāhmaṇas one attains all the worlds; for truth is placed within her, as also brahman and austerity.

sanskrit: vaśāṃ devā upa jīvanti vaśāṃ manuṣyā uta | vaśedaṃ sarvam abhavad yāvat sūryo vipaśyati ||
english: The gods live by the barren cow, and likewise human beings. All this that the sun surveys has come to be through the barren cow.
The joints [of the sacrificial animal] are whose kindling-materials; the Ṛc verses are whose recitation.

sanskrit: chandāṃsi yasya lomāni paristaraṇam id dhavir yajur hṛdayam ucyate ||
english: The metres are whose hairs; the spreading-layer indeed is the oblation; the Yajus is declared to be whose heart.

sanskrit: yad atithipatir atithīn pratipaśyati devayajanaṃ prekṣate ||
english: When the host beholds his guests, he is beholding the divine sacrificial ground.

sanskrit: yad abhivadati dīkṣām upaiti yad udakaṃ yācaty apaḥ pra ṇayati | yā yajñā apaḥ praṇīyante tā eva tāḥ ||
english: When he greets them, he enters consecration; when he asks for water and leads forward the waters — those very waters that are led forward at sacrifices, those are they.

sanskrit: yat tarpaṇam āharanti yo 'gnīṣomīyaḥ paśur badhyate sa eva saḥ ||
english: When they bring the refreshing offering, that is indeed the beast sacred to Agni and Soma that is bound.

sanskrit: yat khātam āharanti puroḍāśā eva tau yad āvasathān kalpayanti sadohavirdhānāny eva tat kalpayanti ||
english: When they bring the excavated [vessel], those two are the rice-cakes; when they arrange the guest-halls, they are thereby arranging the sacrificial hall and the oblation-sheds.
When they spread the underlayer, that is the sacred grass indeed.

sanskrit: yat kaśipūpabarhaṇāny āharanti paridhaya eva te | yad upariśayanam āharanti svargam eva tena lokam ava rundhe ||
english: When they bring the mats and cushions, those are the enclosing sticks; when they bring the upper coverlet, by that one obtains the heavenly world.

sanskrit: yad abhyañjanam āharanty ājyam eva tat | yad aśanakṛtaṃ hvayanti haviṣkṛtam eva tad u hvayanti | yad vrīhayo yad yavā nirupyante aṃśava eva te ny upyante ||
english: When they bring the anointing substance, that is the clarified butter indeed; when they invoke [the guests] for eating, they are thereby invoking for the prepared oblation; when rice-grains and barley-grains are strewn, those stalks are what are strewn.

sanskrit: ulūkhalaṃ musalaṃ grāvāṇau śūrpaṃ pavitraṃ tūṣā ṛjīṣaḥ | srug darvir mekṣaṇam āyavanam āpo 'bhiṣavaṇī yad droṇakalaśaḥ kumbhī ||
english: The mortar, the pestle, the pressing-stones, the winnowing fan, the strainer, the husks, the Soma-residue; the sacrificial ladle, the wooden spoon, the stirring-rod, the mixing-vessel, the waters, the pressing-board, the trough-jar, the water-pot —

sanskrit: idam eva kṛṣṇājinaṃ vāyavyāni pātrāṇi | yajamānaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ vā etad atithipatir kṛṇute yad āhāryāṇy avekṣata idaṃ bhūyā idām iti ||
english: This very black antelope skin, the vessels consecrated to Vāyu — the host makes of these the sacrificer or the Brāhmaṇa, when he looks upon the things that are to be carried [for the guests], saying: 'May this be more, may this [be enough].'

sanskrit: yad āha bhūya uddhareti prajāṃ caiva tena paśūṃś ca vardhayate prāṇam eva tena varṣīyāṃsaṃ kṛṇute | yat saṃpṛcchati kāmam eva tenāva rundhe kāmaṃ hi pṛṣṭo yācati ||
english: When he says 'Bring up more,' by that he increases progeny and cattle; by that he makes breath the greater. When he inquires [after the guests' desires], by that he obtains desire itself — for one who is asked out of regard does request what he desires.

sanskrit: yad udakam abhiṣiñcaty apa eva tenāva rundhe | yad upaharati havīṃṣy ā sādayati ||
english: When he sprinkles water, by that he obtains the waters themselves; when he presents [gifts], he establishes the oblations.

sanskrit: teṣām āsannānām atithir ātmani juhoti | srukkāreṇa vaṣatkāreṇa srucā hastena prāṇe yūpe ||
english: When they are seated, the guest pours the oblation into himself — with the act of the ladle, with the vaṣaṭ-call, with the sacrificial spoon [that is] the hand, into the breath [that is] the sacrificial post.
